page: Microsoft Azure D96d_v5 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the DDv5 family, powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor. It features 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity stands at 384.0 GB, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance includes 3686 GB of local SSD storage, while lacking any dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 93,235.13 and a PassMark CPU score of 76,819.32. Cryptographic capabilities are highly efficient, as demonstrated by a top-tier PassMark CPU encryption score of 87,610.78, aided by hardware-accelerated AES and VAES instruction sets. Memory bandwidth is also robust, reaching 315.9 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 134.24 GB/sec for write operations. However, single-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,646.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1,896.19.

The server exhibits a clear tradeoff between high-throughput parallel processing and sequential execution. While multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 415.94 GB/sec, single-threaded gzip compression is limited to 28.08 GB/sec. Similarly, while prompt processing for small LLM models is strong at 2,398.76 tokens/sec, text generation for large 70B models is weak at 2.69 tokens/sec due to the lack of GPU acceleration. Given these characteristics, the D96d_v5 is suited for multi-threaded workloads such as database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring substantial local SSD storage.
